title: Day 8 of my paper-trading bot competition: a rough Monday where one stock hit most of the strategies, but Strategy 1 finished green and climbed to second
author: DadsGamesandCharles
selftext:
Quick recap for anyone new: over the past year I've built a bunch of AI trading bots, and on Oct 22 I started a public paper-money competition with 13 accounts at $5,000 each (10 strategies, an account that follows Charles 2.0, which is a prediction engine that posts its up-picks before the open, an AI agent's account called Brokgot, and my own hand-traded account). This is the day 8 update, covering everything through the Nov 2 close, the first day of week two.



Everything below is paper money. Nobody steps in to fix the accounts.



Quick note on my hand-traded account: Profit is still in SNAP.



Top 3 accounts so far (by total return since the start)



1. Strategy 9: +$1,010.85 (+20.22%), equity $6,010.85

2. Strategy 1: +$285.16 (+5.70%), equity $5,285.16

3. Charles 2.0: +$78.23 (+1.56%), equity $5,078.23



Results so far (paper money, starting balance $5,000 each)



Daily numbers are the change in account equity each day, from Alpaca's account history, and totals are measured from the Oct 21 close. Oct 22 was the first full day. Every account was out of its positions by the 4:00 PM close today, so today's numbers are the regular-session result. Housekeeping note: the Oct 30 figures each came in somewhere between 6 and 62 cents lower than in my last post after Alpaca finalized its end-of-day numbers, so a few totals won't line up to the penny with Friday.

Brokgot sat this one out. It tried to short CCL a few minutes after the open, but the order was canceled without filling, so it finished flat. CCL ended up closing above where it opened, so missing that one wasn't a bad thing.



SPY for comparison



SPY, close to close: Oct 22 -1.18%, Oct 23 -0.52%, Oct 26 +0.71%, Oct 27 +0.56%, Oct 28 +0.34%, Oct 29 -0.38%, Oct 30 -1.77%, Nov 2 -0.48%. From the Oct 21 close to the Nov 2 close, SPY is down about 2.72%. Over the same stretch the 10 strategies combined are down 3.60% in paper dollars, and the 10 strategies plus Charles 2.0 are down 3.13%.



I said I'd tell you if the bots fell behind SPY, so here it is: after today the combined numbers are behind SPY, by a bit under a point. Eight sessions is still a small sample, and I'm not going to pretend one day decides anything either way, but that's where it stands tonight.



Today, Nov 2: a red day



This one stung. SPY only slipped 0.48%, but the 10 strategies combined gave back $5,587.78, by far their worst day so far. Strategy 1 was the one bright spot, up $104.12 (+2.01%) and now second overall. Charles 2.0 lost just $39.18 and moved up to third. The other nine strategies all finished red, most of them down between 11% and 14% on the day.



Almost all of the damage came from AGX. It opened at its high of the day and slid for most of the session, closing more than 5% below the open, and every strategy that traded it lost money on it. The accounts that held it into the afternoon took the biggest hits, while Strategy 3 and Strategy 7 were out of it within the first 20 minutes and lost far less on it.



The good news is that AEHR mostly worked. It ran up about 2.45% above the open by 10:42 AM before falling hard later in the day, and eight of the ten strategies made money on it, led by Strategy 9 at +$469.63. Strategy 9 had a -$597.46 day overall but is still well out in front at +20.22%.

How Charles 2.0's picks did today



There were four picks today. For each one I checked whether the stock's high for the day, between the 9:30 AM open and 3:59 PM, reached +0.25%, +0.5% and +1.0% above the 9:30 AM open, using minute bars.



1. AEHR: high +2.45% above the open. Touched all three levels.

2. AGX: high +0.00% above the open. The open was its high for the day, so it didn't reach any of the three levels.

3. BRKR: high +0.22% above the open. Didn't reach any of the three levels, just missing +0.25%.

4. NWL: high +16.47% above the open. Touched all three levels.



So two of four touched +0.25%, +0.5% and +1.0%, and two never got going. NWL was the standout, running more than 16% above the open by early afternoon, but none of the accounts traded it today. AGX is the flip side: a pick that went straight down from the open, and that's what cost the strategies today.



Running tally for live Charles 2.0 picks, Sep 22 through Nov 2 (30 sessions, 120 picks): 104 touched +0.25% above the open (87%), 95 touched +0.5% (79%), and 77 touched +1.0% (64%). What I care about is whether a pick reaches those levels during the day, since I want the money that same day, not the next.



Keeping it honest



Eight sessions is still a short stretch, and some people have had doubts about the strategies, which is fair. That's exactly why this is happening in public, red days included, and today was a big red one. Days like this are exactly what I want to learn from, and I'd rather see them now on paper than later with real money.



A few people asked about the strategy: I'm keeping the exact rules to myself, but the bots all start from the same morning picks and differ in how they get in and out.



What's next



Daily results after each close, and a fuller write-up as the sample grows. See you tomorrow.



Questions you probably have



Is this real money? No. Every account is paper money.



Is paper trading realistic? Not entirely. Paper can't show market impact, and real fills are usually worse. That's the main reason my early backtests got cut down.



Will you ever trade real money? Yes, we will.



Can I buy or subscribe to anything? Not yet.



Is this financial advice? No. The picks are research ideas to watch, not tips, and nothing here is a guarantee of anything.



Are AI agents involved? Yes. AI agents help build, test and run the bots, and one of the accounts is traded by an AI agent. I'm the one who reviews and posts this.



Why publish bad numbers? Because a track record that only shows the good days isn't worth much.



What if a bot loses? Then it loses in public. The accounts are paper and no one steps in to fix them.



Why did the competition start on Oct 22? Earlier starts on Monday and Tuesday had account setup problems, so those days don't count.



Where can I follow along? On this profile. I'll post daily results here after the close.



Have a question that isn't here? Ask in the comments and I'll answer it.



Paper money only. Not financial advice. Written with help from AI.

comments.author: TrustedEssentials
comments.body: Was S9’s AGX loss from one trade or multiple entries? And did it stay in until the 3:55 exit, or get out earlier?

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
Multiple entries, but it was the third trade that got him. Before that the account was up nicely lol

He held onto like a Heisman all the way until 355pm per his programming.

replies.author: TrustedEssentials
replies.body: Got it. What were S9’s three trades in order that day, with roughly the entry/exit times and position sizes? Trying to understand how the earlier gains turned into the AGX loss.

replies.author: DadsGamesandCharles
replies.body:
AEHR were the previous trades before AGX.

AGX is a different stock on its list of 4 for the day and the 4 turn doesn’t just use 1 of the 4 for all the buys.

So an AEHR gain turned into an AGX loss because that’s how the stocks lined up for the day to be traded.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Thanks for posting the bad day with the full table, and for saying plainly that the bots fell behind SPY. The day also shows the same thing as before: nearly every account traded the same two stocks, so one pick going wrong hit almost all of them at once. That makes the ten accounts closer to one bet than ten. I'd check how many different stocks drive the results over the next few weeks. For the AI agent side, Cymetica's Bring Your Own Agent runs agents in paper mode on a practice balance.
